It also directly violated key ticket decisions and acceptance criteria: it did not implement the `transport.history: {enabled: boolean}` opt-in flag (serving lists unconditionally), returned an empty list instead of the required `UNSUPPORTED` error code when a store lacks `listFor`, and allowed `limit: 0` or `limit > 200` in validation instead of enforcing 1–200. Furthermore, it logged raw store error messages on failure (which the ticket explicitly warns against), left `.lore/dod.md` committed in the tree, and missed updating `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md`, `example/full-config.ts`, and `docs/getting-started.md`. On the positive side, the candidate did wire `sessionStore` into `createMessageHandler` off the per-session turn lock, validated the composite `{updatedAt, sessionId}` cursor, and ignored client-supplied `userId` fields.
